clue.text: Type of music from the South side

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for south
a wing is a side section of a building or a team's flank

explanation.surface: A style of music said to come from the southern part of a country.
explanation.definitionFit: Swing is the big-band jazz style of the 1930s and 1940s, a genre of popular music.

clue.text: Italian composer exposed in trial, acts strangely

indicators.note: strangely means in an odd way, so the letters appear in an unusual order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A composer on trial behaves oddly in court.
explanation.definitionFit: Domenico Scarlatti was the Neapolitan baroque composer famous for his hundreds of keyboard sonatas.

clue.text: At the start, leading article's suppressed

indicators.note: something suppressed is kept in, so the word is read as being in

parts.note: the definite article 'is suppressed', that is, is in
a leader is in first place

explanation.surface: A newspaper's editorial has been censored from the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading article' looks like an editorial, but leading and article split apart. Article is THE, and the article being suppressed is read as 'in THE', placed before the phrase for leading.
explanation.definitionFit: In the first place is an idiom meaning originally or to begin with, the same as at the start.

clue.text: Golfer's opener — Rose possibly in the furze

indicators.note: an opener comes first, so only the opening letter of the word is used

parts.note: the first letter of golfer

indicators.note: possibly suggests one of several arrangements, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A golfer's first shot, perhaps by Justin Rose, lands in the rough.
explanation.walkthrough: Justin Rose is an English golfer, which makes 'Rose' look like a name rather than letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Furze is another name for gorse, the spiny yellow-flowered shrub of heaths and golf-course rough.

clue.text: King in America meeting important stars

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it sits inside it, enclosed by the other letters

parts.note: the United States of America
R for Rex, Latin for king
major means significant or important

explanation.surface: A king visiting the United States meets some important celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stars' looks like famous people, which fits the king's visit, but here it means a group of actual stars in the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Ursa Major, the Great Bear, is a constellation, a named pattern of stars in the northern sky.

clue.text: A French counterfeit coin carrying head of Richelieu and a mythical animal

parts.note: un is French for a

indicators.note: carrying means holding something within, so the next piece goes inside
a counterfeit is a fake made up to look real, so the word is reworked

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so only that one is taken

parts.note: the first letter of Richelieu

explanation.surface: A forged French coin bearing Cardinal Richelieu's head and a legendary beast.
explanation.walkthrough: COIN rearranged becomes ICON, which then holds R before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The unicorn is a legendary horse-like creature with a single horn, a classic beast of myth.

clue.text: Mad sort, eccentric achieving fame

indicators.note: eccentric means off-centre and odd, so the letters are knocked out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A crazy, odd character becomes a celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: Stardom is the status of being a celebrity, so it is synonymous with fame.

clue.text: Distinguished conductor describing Latin mass in turmoil

indicators.note: to describe a circle is to draw round it, so this word goes round the next

parts.note: a maestro is an eminent conductor
L is the abbreviation for Latin
M is the symbol for mass in physics

explanation.surface: A famous conductor talks about a Latin Mass amid chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Describing' looks like talking about, but here it means drawing round: MAESTRO goes round L, then M follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A maelstrom is a violent whirlpool, and figuratively any scene of confused turmoil.

clue.text: A daft joker's call upset handyman

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A silly prankster's phone call annoyed the odd-job man.
explanation.definitionFit: A jack of all trades is a person who can turn a hand to many jobs, exactly a versatile handyman.

clue.text: Swift attack round centre of Tripoli

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the first word encloses the next

parts.note: a raid is a surprise attack

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the middle of the seven letters of Tripoli

explanation.surface: A quick military strike around the middle of the Libyan capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapid means fast-moving or quick, a straightforward synonym for swift.

clue.text: Amputation scare turned out to be much ado about nothing

indicators.note: something turned out has been flipped and rearranged, so the letters come in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, fifteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A patient's fear of losing a limb proves to be a false alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition borrows the title of Shakespeare's comedy, lower-cased so it reads as a plain phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A storm in a teacup is an idiom for a big fuss over something trivial, exactly a great commotion over nothing.

clue.text: Tell untruths about e.g. praise, reportedly for a feudal superior

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word wraps round the next one

parts.note: to lie is to tell untruths
taken as written

indicators.note: reportedly means as told or heard, so the word is taken by how it is said

parts.note: to laud is to praise; in non-rhotic British speech it rhymes with the noble title

explanation.surface: Someone lies about praising their medieval overlord.
explanation.walkthrough: The sound-alike works for speakers who do not pronounce the R in the noble title, as in standard British English.
explanation.definitionFit: A liege lord was the noble to whom a vassal owed allegiance and service under the feudal system.

clue.text: Son's term for a weapon

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
a term is a word

explanation.surface: A boy's name for some kind of weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of Son's means 'has' or 'is', just joining S to the next piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A sword is a bladed hand weapon, a classic example of an arm.

clue.text: Training out in it abroad

indicators.note: abroad can mean scattered widely or astray, so the letters are spread into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Coaching that takes place overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuition is teaching or instruction, so it is the same thing as training given to a learner.

clue.text: Ones imprisoned by one country or another

definitions.note: another country, following on from 'one country'

indicators.note: something imprisoned is locked up inside, so these letters go within the next

parts.note: India is one country
taken as written

explanation.surface: People locked up by one nation or other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One country or another' reads as a vague phrase, but it splits: the first country is the container and 'another' is the definition, a second country.
explanation.definitionFit: Indonesia is a nation of Southeast Asia, so it is another country besides India.

clue.text: Royal Marines, first-rate, captivated by sea siren

indicators.note: being captivated by something means being held by it, so these letters are held inside

parts.note: the Med, short for the Mediterranean Sea
RM is the abbreviation for Royal Marines
A1 means first-rate, with the one written as I

explanation.surface: Marines are entranced by a sea siren's song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sea siren' looks like one phrase, but sea is wordplay and siren alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sirens and mermaids are both alluring sea creatures of legend, half woman, who lure sailors.

clue.text: Wife and child avoiding one in farm building

parts.note: 'my old Dutch' is Cockney slang for one's wife

indicators.note: avoiding something means keeping it out, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: bairn is the Scottish and northern English word for a child
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A wife and child keep away from someone in a farm building.
explanation.walkthrough: The I is removed from the child word.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dutch barn is an open-sided barn with a curved roof on posts, used on farms to store hay.

clue.text: One of us behind bars beginning to reform

parts.note: someone behind bars is inside, in prison slang

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the first letter of reform

explanation.surface: A prisoner, one of our own, starting to mend their ways.
explanation.definitionFit: An insider is a member of a group, someone within the circle rather than an outsider.

clue.text: Free of jungle yet? Every second counts for displaced person

indicators.note: only every second letter counts, so letters two, four, six and so on are kept

parts.note: the even-placed letters of these words

explanation.surface: Someone escaping the jungle, where every second matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Every second counts' reads as a stock phrase about urgency, but it literally picks the second, fourth, sixth letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A refugee is someone forced to flee their home, the standard meaning of a displaced person.

clue.text: Arrived at film studio to make a musical

parts.note: came means arrived
a lot is the land of a film studio, as in the back lot

explanation.surface: Someone turned up at a studio to shoot a film musical.
explanation.definitionFit: Camelot is the Lerner and Loewe stage show about King Arthur's court, a well-known musical.

clue.text: Artist in court worried guardian

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so these letters go within the next
worried can mean shaken about, as a dog worries a bone, so the letters are tossed

parts.note: taken as written
RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts

explanation.surface: A painter in the dock is anxious about their guardian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' looks like a law court with an artist on trial, but it is just letters to be rearranged around the painter.
explanation.definitionFit: A curator is a keeper or custodian, such as of a museum collection, so in effect a guardian.

clue.text: Tree evident in Colorado ski resort

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a poplar with trembling leaves
second meaning: the fashionable mountain town in the Rockies

explanation.surface: Trees that can be seen around a ski resort in the Rockies.
explanation.walkthrough: The resort was in fact named after the trees growing on its slopes.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspen is both a quaking poplar species and the famous Colorado mountain town known for skiing.

clue.text: Collect a million as head of security

parts.note: taken as written
M is the abbreviation for million
taken as written

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so only that is taken

parts.note: the first letter of security

explanation.surface: A security chief gathers a million.
explanation.definitionFit: To amass is to gather together or accumulate, the same as to collect a lot of something.

clue.text: Blockhouse's value in a Texas city

parts.note: a blockhouse is a small fort
worth means value

explanation.surface: What a fortification is worth somewhere in Texas.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's just hangs the two halves together, as in a fort's worth.
explanation.definitionFit: Fort Worth is a large city in north Texas, next to Dallas.

clue.text: Chess player with involved ending in game

indicators.note: involved means tangled and complicated, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its final letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the last letter of game

explanation.surface: A chess player gets caught up in the endgame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ending in game' looks like the chess endgame but just picks a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess, White is the player with the light pieces, who moves first.

clue.text: Novel's fantastic a poet's said again

indicators.note: fantastic means fanciful or bizarre, so the letters are reworked in an unlikely way

parts.note: taken as written, every letter used

explanation.surface: A book praised as wonderful by a poet repeating himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like an adjective meaning new, but it is the noun: a work of fiction.
explanation.definitionFit: A Passage to India is E. M. Forster's 1924 novel set during British rule in India.

clue.text: Cry, cut biting fruit

indicators.note: something biting holds another thing between its jaws, so the second word goes inside

parts.note: to shear is to cut
a date is the fruit of the date palm

explanation.surface: Someone weeps after slicing into a piece of fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: To shed a tear is to weep, an idiom matching the verb sense of crying.

clue.text: Some process engineering in German industrial city

indicators.note: some means only part of what follows, so the letters lie within those words

parts.note: the end of process runs into the start of engineering

explanation.surface: Manufacturing done in a German factory town.
explanation.definitionFit: Essen is a city in the Ruhr, Germany's heavy-industry heartland, long home of the Krupp steelworks.
